body.p: I. Introduction

Upon entry of the present amendment, claims 1, 4, 5, 8-16, and 20-23 will be pending in this application. Claims 1, 21, and 22 have been amended, claim 19 has been canceled without prejudice or disclaimer, and new claim 23 has been added. Support for amendments can be found at least in FIGS. 2-3 of the published application. No new matter is added. Based on the following remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims.
II. Drawing Objection

The drawings are objected to a line pointing to a footrest with no numbering. FIG. 4 has been amended to include reference number "209" pointing to the footrest. Accordingly, Applicant requests reconsideration and withdrawal of drawing objection.
III. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. & 112

Claims 1, 4-5, 8-16, and 19-22 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) and § 112(b) as due to the term "continuous surface" for reasons noted in the office action at pages 2-3. Without acknowledging the propriety of rejections, Applicant has amended the claims to delete the term "continuous" solely to expediate prosecution. Accordingly, Applicant requests reconsideration and withdrawal of § 112 rejections.
IV. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. & 102 & & 103

Claims 1, 4-5, 8-10, and 21 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. 10,501,188 B2 to Nicholas et al. ("Nicholas") or, in the alternative, under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2013/0241247 Al to Wallace et al. ("Wallace"), in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,312,494 B2 to O'Neill et al. ("O'Neill"). Claims 11 and 13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas, or alternatively over Nicholas in view of Wallace, in view of O'Neill as applied to claim 1 above, in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,794,902 B2 to Pothier ("Pothier"). Claims 11-12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being

unpatentable over Nicholas in view of Pothier, or alternatively over Nicholas in view of Wallace, in view of O'Neill, in view of Pothier as applied to claim 1 above, in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2013/0126671 Al to Guering ("Guering"). Claims 14-16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas, or alternatively over Nicholas in view of Wallace, in view of O'Neil as applied to claim 1 above, in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2017/0283064 Al to Robinson ("Robinson"). Claim 20 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas, or alternatively over Nicholas in view of Wallace, in view of O'Neil, in view of Pothier as applied to claim 1 above. Claim 22 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas in view of Wallace, in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,299,274 B1 to Davis et al. ("Davis") or alternatively in view of Wallace in view of Pothier, in view of O'Neil. Applicant traverses this rejection and requests its withdrawal.
Independent claim 1 has been amended solely to expedite prosecution of this case. Claim 1, as amended, inter alia, recites:
...wherein the seat unit does not include a leg rest extending
from the seat,
the seat comprises a seat pan without the leg rest directly
extending from the seat pan, and backrest...
...in the second position of the seat the front edge of the seat
pan touches the footrest such that the footrest and seat pan together
form a surface without the leg rest
The cited references fail to teach or suggest all the features recited in amended claim 1.

Support for the amended claims can be found at least in the figures of the as-filed specification. For example, FIG. 1 clearly shows the seat unit does not include a leg rest directly extending from the seat pan 119. FIGS. 2-3 clearly shows the front edge of the seat pan touches the footrest in the second position.

Nicholas describes a seat unit having a seat pan 515b, a leg rest 515c, and an ottoman 526 of a foot-receiving structure 523, see FIG. Sd below for references. The 3-pieces 515b, 515c, and 526 of the seat unit cooperate to form a coplanar "transfer surface" to allow disabled-access configuration. Additionally, an end wall 525 can be removed (and later reattached) to widen an opening 533 from 13 inches to 20 inches. In another embodiments, in FIG. 7a-7d, the end wall 725 is slidable to widen the opening to 20 inches.
On the contrary, the claimed seat unit does not have a leg rest (as amended above) as the seat pan 209 touches the footrest 219 (shaded in blue), as shown in FIG. 2 (see below) and FIG.
3 of the present application.
SVG {EMBED HERE} 3.385.437Fig. 5d Nicholas Fig. 2 Present application

Wallace does shows a seat bottom 16 touches the ottoman 18 and does not have a leg rest. However, Nicholas cannot reasonably be modified in view of Wallace because none of the embodiments suggest the leg rest in Nicholas can be removed, rather it is part of the 3-piece seat unit (seat pan, leg rest, and ottoman) sized for disabled access function e.g., for creating coplanar transfer surface. Even assuming arguendo the leg rest is removed, the seat size or ottoman size of Nicholas will increase significantly preventing disabled access and will not be able to meet a minimum 13 inches access opening in normal configuration, thereby violating purpose of Nicholas. If a smaller seat size is used, the seat back of Nicholas will need to be in lie-flat position to create the planar transfer surface, rather than in an upright position as intended by Nicholas. This can be undesirable for disabled access requiring an upright seat back.
For at least the reasons presented above, Applicant respectfully submits that amended independent claim 1 is not anticipated or rendered obvious by Nicholas, Wallace, or other cited
references, alone or in combination. Independent claim 21 and 22 similarly recites

aforementioned features of claim 1, and as such these claims are also believed allowable for similar reasons as above. Dependent claims are believed allowable at least due to their dependence from the independent claim 1 as well as the features they recite individually. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the 35 U.S.C. § 102 and § 103 rejections be withdrawn and that these claims be allowed.
V. New Claims

Claim 23 is new. Support for this new claim can be found, for example, in the FIG. 2. No new matter has been added. Applicant submits that claim 23 is allowable at least for the reason of its dependence upon allowable base claim 1 and for the reason that its additional recitals further distinguish them from the cited references.

For example, the cited references cannot reasonably be combined to describe "the movable panel is configured to rotate into the aisle when moving from the closed position to the open position" to provide access to footrest.

Nicholas, in FIGs. 7a-d, shows the wall 725 is slidable to "widen the access opening from 13 inches to 20 inches" in the disabled-access configuration. In another embodiment of FIG. 5a, discussed above, the wall 525 is removable. Nowhere does Nicholas suggest the wall 525 or 725 can open into the aisle. None of the other references show a panel hingedly coupled to open into the aisle.

Pethier, in FIG. 5, shows the wall 80 is rotatable, but it rotates inward, not into the aisle. For example, Pethier clearly recites "In the opened position, the reconfigurable wall element 80 is pivoted so that the second edge 84 is interior to the lavatory enclosure 14." Walls of lavatory enclosure are very different from wall of a seat unit at least in terms of size and functional limitations. A person of ordinary skill will not be motivated to modify a slidable wall or a removable wall of a seat unit (in Nicholas) to a rotatable wall of a lavatory. Such modification can require substantial structural modifications to the seat structure because seat spacing is very limited, and includes other seat components/accessories (e.g., console, monitor, etc.) which may also need modification. Secondly, modifying Nicholas' slidable wall 725 to a rotatable wall will not guarantee the wider access from 13 inches to 20 inches, which is required in the disabled- access configuration. Even assuming, arguendo, Nicholas is modified in view of Pethier, the
panel has to move inward, not into the aisle, which defeats the purpose of Nicholas of having wide opening.
Favorable consideration of this new claim is respectfully requested.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant believes all claims now pending in this application are in condition for allowance. The issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance at an early date is respectfully requested.
